claims.claim: A B.C. Supreme Court judge signed an order forfeiting the 66-hectare property at 5011 Hoath Rd. in Falkland to the director of civil forfeiture.
claims.episode_span: forfeiting the 66-hectare property at 5011 Hoath Rd. in Falkland
claims.source_title: Falkland fentanyl lab property forfeited to the B.C. government
claims.supporting_quote: Last week, a B.C. Supreme Court judge signed an order that the 66-hectare property at 5011 Hoath Rd. would be forfeited to the province’s director of civil forfeiture.

claims.claim: Five per cent of the net proceeds of any sale of the Falkland property is to be paid to owner Michael Driehuyzen, who was never charged.
claims.episode_span: five per cent of the net proceeds of any sale goes to him as partial relief
claims.source_title: Falkland fentanyl lab property forfeited to the B.C. government
claims.supporting_quote: The consent order, signed by a lawyer for owner Michael Driehuyzen, allows for five per cent of the net proceeds of any sale to be paid to Driehuyzen as “partial relief.”

claims.claim: Officers seized 52 kilograms of fentanyl and several tonnes of precursor chemicals, which a senior Mountie said could have produced 95 million doses.
claims.episode_span: officers seized 52 kilograms of fentanyl and several tonnes of precursor chemicals
claims.source_title: Falkland fentanyl lab property forfeited to the B.C. government
claims.supporting_quote: Officers seized 52 kilograms of fentanyl and several tonnes of precursor chemicals from the property.

claims.claim: Effingham Island recorded 469 millimetres of rain from 11 a.m. Monday to 1 p.m. Wednesday, Kennedy Lake recorded 261 millimetres, and Estevan Point recorded 110.
claims.episode_span: recorded 469 millimetres of rain from 11 a.m. Monday to 1 p.m. Wednesday
claims.source_title: Weather station records 469 millimetres of rain in latest B.C. soaking
claims.supporting_quote: A weather summary provided by the agency says the Effingham Island station recorded the rain from 11 a.m. on Monday to 1 p.m. on Wednesday.

claims.claim: The Comox Valley Regional District and the City of Courtenay issued evacuation alerts, and a flood watch was issued for eastern Vancouver Island.
claims.episode_span: the Comox Valley Regional District and the City of Courtenay issued evacuation alerts
claims.source_title: Weather station records 469 millimetres of rain in latest B.C. soaking
claims.supporting_quote: Late Wednesday, the Comox Valley Regional District and the City of Courtenay have issued Evacuation Alerts, while the provincial river forecast centre issued a flood watch for eastern Vancouver Island

claims.claim: New Democrats are sworn in Thursday without David Eby, who won Vancouver-Point Grey and will be sworn in separately, according to Jennifer Whiteside.
claims.episode_span: former premier David Eby, who won Vancouver-Point Grey, is not among them
claims.source_title: NDP caucus to take oath in Victoria while Eby to be sworn in separately
claims.supporting_quote: Jennifer Whiteside, interim leader of the B.C. New Democrats, says Eby will be sworn in separately as he is taking some time to step back to “reflect.”

claims.claim: The Conservatives won 64 seats, the NDP 27 and the Greens two after Eby called a snap election two years early.
claims.episode_span: the Conservatives hold 64 seats, the NDP 27 and the Greens two
claims.source_title: NDP caucus to take oath in Victoria while Eby to be sworn in separately
claims.supporting_quote: Eby called the snap election two years early, reducing his party to official Opposition status with 27 seats, while the Conservatives won 64 seats and the Greens have two members.

claims.claim: B.C. Transit and the Greater Victoria transit union meet Thursday ahead of a possible day-long strike Friday.
claims.episode_span: meet today, ahead of a scheduled day-long strike that could shut down the region's transit system on Friday
claims.source_title: B.C. Transit, union meet ahead of looming Greater Victoria transit strike
claims.supporting_quote: B.C. Transit and the union representing Greater Victoria transit workers will meet Thursday, ahead of a scheduled day-long strike that could shut down the region's transit system on Friday.

claims.claim: Shane Ertmoed was granted a two-month unescorted absence from Dec. 1 for cooking classes at a Victoria-area residential facility.
claims.episode_span: a two-month unescorted absence, starting Dec. 1, to take cooking classes
claims.source_title: As B.C. child killer leaves prison, mother of victim calls for changes to system
claims.supporting_quote: Shane Ertmoed will be allowed to leave prison on Dec. 1 to attend a two-month cooking program while living at a community residential facility in the Victoria area, according to a recent decision by the Parole Board of Canada.

claims.claim: Mike Hurley will not seek re-election as Metro Vancouver Regional District board chair, with a new chair elected Friday.
claims.episode_span: will not seek re-election as board chair of the Metro Vancouver Regional District
claims.source_title: Burnaby Mayor Mike Hurley to step down as board chair of Metro Vancouver Regional District
claims.supporting_quote: Mike Hurley will not seek re-election as board chair of the Metro Vancouver Regional District, and a new board chair will be elected from among a number of elected municipal leaders on Friday.

claims.claim: Surrey's chief election officer petitioned to avoid a byelection after Garry Thind was re-elected trustee and elected MLA, at a cost of nearly $840,000.
claims.episode_span: puts the cost of a byelection at nearly $840,000
claims.source_title: Court to decide whether Surrey holds costly byelection to fill vacant school trustee seat
claims.supporting_quote: The total cost to hold a byelection would amount to nearly $840,000, according to an affidavit from Surrey's city clerk.

claims.claim: Premier Lorne Doerkson said the government will keep smaller-community ERs and maternity wards open with flexible staffing and a $50-million rural health emergency fund.
claims.source_title: B.C. premier pledges to bolster health-care staffing as woman dies outside closed ER
claims.supporting_quote: Lorne Doerkson said his new government will keep ERs and maternity wards open in smaller B.C. communities through flexible staffing and a $50-million rural health emergency fund.

claims.claim: Nov. 24, 2026 mandate letters direct ministers to end safe supply, expand drug courts, and review overdose prevention and injection sites, with no end date given.
claims.episode_span: Mandate letters dated Nov. 24, 2026 tell them to end that approach to drug use
claims.source_title: B.C. premier moves to end safe supply, expand treatment and toughen enforcement
claims.supporting_quote: The provincial government will now “end the ‘safe supply’ approach to drug use; expand drug courts; move funding to prevention, treatment and recovery; stop forcing drug-friendly facilities on communities; and review and reform overdose prevention sites (OPS) and injection sites.”

claims.claim: In Vancouver's October 2026 election, 68 per cent backed a secure treatment facility ask and nearly 69 per cent backed stronger open-air drug laws, and the new council signalled it will not act on either.
claims.episode_span: 68 per cent of voters backed asking the province to turn part of the old St. Paul's Hospital campus
claims.source_title: B.C. premier moves to end safe supply, expand treatment and toughen enforcement
claims.supporting_quote: Despite that support, the new left-leaning Vancouver City Council has strongly signalled that it does not intend to act on either plebiscite result.

claims.claim: The Canucks lost 5-2 to the Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday, ending Brock Boeser's 11-game point streak, while extending a 38-game scoring run.
claims.episode_span: The Canucks lost 5-2 to the Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday
claims.source_title: I Watched This Game: Canucks are keeping alive an impressive streak this season
claims.supporting_quote: It’s very easy to focus on the negative after the Vancouver Canucks lost 5-2 to the Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday night.

claims.claim: An orange coastal flooding warning is in effect for Vancouver, with Thursday's high 12 and southeast wind 40 km/h gusting to 60.
claims.episode_span: An orange coastal flooding warning is in effect for Vancouver
claims.supporting_quote: Thursday: Showers ending early this afternoon then cloudy with 60 percent chance of showers. Risk of thunderstorms this morning. Wind southeast 40 km/h gusting to 60. High 12.

claims.claim: Highway 1 is closed from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford until Dec. 31, 2026, with a detour.
claims.episode_span: Highway 1 is closed from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford until Dec. 31, 2026
claims.source_title: DriveBC: 4 major road events in Metro Vancouver
claims.supporting_quote: Road construction from Highway 1, In Langley - District and 256th Street to In Abbotsford and Lefeuvre Road. Starting 12:00 AM PDT on Friday October 30, 2026 until 12:00 AM PCT on Thursday December 31, 2026. All day, every day. Closed. Detour in effect.

claims.claim: Doerkson's Nov. 24 mandate letter directs legislation restoring public access to Crown land, expected in the spring 2027 session, against the backdrop of Joffre Lakes closures.
claims.episode_span: restoring public access to Crown land, beaches and the backcountry
claims.source_title: New B.C. legislation to restore and protect public access to Crown land
claims.supporting_quote: His mandate letter on Nov. 24, 2026 to Warbus states that access to such Crown areas must be restored “for all British Columbians through legislation, subject only to legitimate conservation and safety requirements.”
